```bash
cp .env.example .env        # ARENA_API_KEY (one team key), LLM_PROVIDER=openai, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena data           # data package into data/package
uv run arena me             # quota left
```
Never commit `.env` or print keys. Entire must stay enabled (`entire enable` after cloning).
Default model `gpt-6-luna` (cheap, fast); compare with `gpt-6.1-sol` later.

## Architecture (all in `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/team/`)
```
case ─► 1 PREPARE  briefing.py   supplier profile + arguments that check out (pure SQL, < 1 s)
     ─► 2 NEGOTIATE agent.py     levers.py (EUR per lever, priced at the supplier's REVEALED slopes from its
                                 own sheet pairs) → planner: fixed anchor, steps of 0/15/30/45/60 % of the C
                                 gap, full coverage locked, 2 equal-cost MESO variants (incl. a payment probe)
                                 → LLM writes the e-mail; code caps sheets to the plan's C band, completes
                                 them from OUR sheet A, drops repeated / unknown IDs. RFQ message 1: no LLM,
                                 cites the cheapest rival offer ID. LLM gets only what is left of the 60 s.
     ─► 3 CLOSE     agent.py     accept LADDER over every sheet ever offered (main + alternatives), cheapest
                                 first; final_offer = accept now (repair message only if nothing is
                                 acceptable); 'agreed' / stall -> its earlier cheaper sheet once; never send a
                                 sheet dearer than one already on the table; never break a must-have
        runner.py                one worker per supplier thread, retries + landing check on network errors,
                                 waits for in-flight rival replies before an accept, done only when the
                                 arena ended the session, closes on the ladder before a wave cap
   (supplier model: full cost = should-cost / 1.02, cash-short only from the supplier's own words)
   4 MEASURE  evaluate.py        runs cases, summary.md per run (score vs previous, missed levers, reasons)
   5 DELIVER  final.py           Live Final runner, --rehearse, --check (pre-flight)
```

## Run (from `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit`)
| What | Command | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Levers of a case | `uv run python -m team.levers case:P01 --price 135.10` | free |
| Briefing of a case | `uv run python -m team.briefing case:P01` | free |
| Simulator (scripted supplier) | `uv run python -m team.evaluate --sim` | free (LLM cents) |
| Sandbox (real demo suppliers D01, D02) | `uv run python -m team.evaluate --set sandbox` | free |
| All 10 practice cases, final-like | `uv run python -m team.evaluate --label <change> --cap 480 --parallel 10` | 10 sessions |
| Offline tests on recorded negotiations | `uv run --group dev pytest team/tests -q` | free, no API |
| Pre-flight | `uv run python -m team.final --check` | free |
| Dress rehearsal | `uv run python -m team.final --rehearse case:D02` | free |
| **Live Final** (start before 12:00, leave running) | `uv run python -m team.final` | - |

Practice score (mean of 10 cases x 100, 8-min cap, `gpt-6-luna`): v2 13.3 (pushed past final offers ->
walk-aways) | v4 56.3 (accept final offers) | v5 56.7 | v6 48.6 / v7 49.5 / v8 42.4 (bugs, fixed) |
**v9 56.9, all 10 deals** | v9 with `gpt-6.1-sol` 58.1 (within noise; luna stays default). Runs vary by
about +-0.2 per case: compare versions on all 10 cases, not on one.
Weakest: P02 (copper index, firm "pricing committee"), P18/P08 (raw material: index clause + base price).

## Learned so far
Offline mining of ~80 recorded practice negotiations (Sat night, no API; rules kept only if seen in >= 3 cases):
- **Message 1 carries ~90 % of the value**: the supplier's reply to it gains +0.46 score on average, replies 2-4
  together +0.08. Put the full structure (coverage, payment variants, rival quote) into message 1.
- **The best sheet ever offered was often not taken** (P01 7/7 runs): taking it would have given 0.586 vs 0.550.
  30 % of supplier replies carry an alternative sheet, 38 % of those are cheaper for us than its main sheet.
- Any message after a `final_offer` -> walked away **8/8**; accepting it -> deal 38/38.
- 12-month packages on a 2-year need: P08 0.08 vs 0.44, P10 volume cut below the must-have 4/4.
- Suppliers charge 3-7x the value for faster lead time / chargebacks -> ask only what the need requires.
- Price-history claims "hold, but do not change our calculation" 41/46 -> context only, not an argument.
- Zero-step messages drew a final offer 37 % of the time, steps >= 15 % of the gap 17 %.
- Suppliers **walk away** when pushed after `final_offer` -> accept it.
- Pushing small levers (e.g. a chargeback worth 0.3 % of C) makes suppliers raise the price far more -> skip them.
- **Uncovered need** is bought at `fallback_unit_price`: expensive in most cases, but cheaper than the offer in
  some (P08: fallback 5.72 < offer 5.98) - the lever table knows which, trust it.
- **One full practice run at a time per team**: the key allows 10 open sessions, a second run gets HTTP 429.
  Say in the team chat before you start one. Quota is now 600 sessions per day.
- In an RFQ every thread has its own 60 s clock; calls on one session queue on the server.
- Open practice sessions count against the 10 open sessions per key -> the final runner closes them first.
- The LLM tends to concede too fast -> code caps every sheet at the planned C.

## Still open (claim by writing your name)
- Kit baseline on all practice cases for the pitch (`--agent llm`, 10 sessions).
- Per-type playbooks: tune with replays (P02 copper index clause, P10 capacity, P18 index deadband).
- Answer supplier questions with data attachments (they ask "which figures?" - md/csv attachments are read).
- Pitch: score progression per version, one replay story (P01 notice-period argument).

## Conventions
- Code in `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/team/` (keep the vendored kit untouched so it can be updated).
- Numbers from code, words from the model. One change per evaluation run; write the label so others see it.
- Commit messages in English, short (`feat: ...`). Pull before push, never `--force`.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests for R5.2-R5.4 (reciprocity, deadlock breaker, still-moving), R6.2-R6.5 (surplus,
  ask sheets, decoy, floor) and R7 (close rules, including "no close on a two-round hold").

  (clock) and R11.17-R11.18 (coverage, every RFQ bidder answered).
- Practice runs, the best of either agent per case: P01 ≥ 0.941, P02 ≥ 0.385, P03 ≥ 0.919,
  P04 ≥ 0.86, P05 ≥ 0.444, P07 ≥ 0.721, P08 ≥ 0.343, P10 ≥ 0.655, P11 ≥ 0.589, P18 ≥ 0.419.

## 12. From TeamAgent

### 12.1 Message 1 carries the deal

- **R12.1 Put the whole structure into the first message.** Mined from ~80 recorded practice
  negotiations (`AGENTS.md`): the supplier's reply to our first message gained +0.46 score on
  average, replies 2-4 together +0.08. The first message already carries full coverage (R12.2), the
  payment variants, the rival's offer (RFQ) and the strongest arguments. Every best TeamAgent run
  (P04, P05, P07, P08, P10) did this.
- **R12.2 Coverage lock.** Commit the full need for the full horizon from message 1 whenever the
  lever table says covering it lowers C (P08: 24 months on a 2-year need; 12-month packages scored

  if it saves us more than the supplier charges for it; on a tie (within EUR 1) take the option closest

  15 % is the size of the deadlock-breaking step (R5.3) and the floor of a step we choose to make;
  the reciprocity cap (R5.2) still limits our step when the supplier moved less.

  case, cut by the goal's share plus 4 points for competition; in an RFQ it may move down when a
  rival goes lower, never up (R4.4 otherwise).

  value, or to 30 days) at equal C: its pick reveals its cost of money (P05: 90/60/30 sheets; the

content.text:
I've added `TeamAgent` to [NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md) as section 12, with an evidence table and new acceptance criteria.

**`TeamAgent` produced 4–5 of the 10 best practice runs.** Its runs aren't in the session log, so I matched them from the replays. Three things identify them: its e-mail signature, its fixed fallback text appearing word for word in P10, and run times that fit its commits. P07 is the least certain.

| Case | TeamAgent | DualAgent | BuyerAgent |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 (RFQ) | **0.781** | 0.444 | 0.372 |
| P08 (raw material) | **0.549** | 0.343 | 0.332 |
| P07 (bundling) | **0.773** | 0.721 | 0.702 |
| P10 (capacity) | **0.671** | 0.655 | 0.655 |
| P04 | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.86 |

**Section 12, what was taken:**
- **Message 1 carries the deal:** full coverage, payment variants, the rival's price and the best arguments all go into the first e-mail. Across ~80 recorded negotiations, the reply to the first message gained +0.46 score on average, against +0.08 for replies 2–4 together. Coverage is locked from message 1 onward.
- **Levers priced in euros:** a lever table in euros that skips levers worth under 0.3% of C. The supplier's own prices for terms are read from pairs of its sheets that differ in one term, so we never ask more than needed.
- **Steps:** every step is at least 15% of the gap left. Messages without a step drew a final offer 37% of the time, steps of 15% or more only 17%. In an RFQ, the anchor only ever falls.
- **Sheets:**
  - a payment probe in the first menu;
  - the supplier's own index series, with the cheapest deadband rather than 0% (P08);
  - a price floor for each package structure;
  - never sending a sheet as costly for us as one the supplier already offered.
- **Closing:**
  - an accept ladder over every sheet ever offered, alternatives included;
  - final offers accepted at once: 8/8 walked away when pushed, 38/38 dealt when accepted;
  - one repair message only if nothing on the table is acceptable;
  - after `agreed`, its earlier cheaper sheet is offered back once.
- **RFQ:** the first message to each bidder is written by code and quotes the cheapest rival's offer. Hopeless bidders are dropped, and before accepting it waits for replies still in flight.
- **Time and robustness:**
  - a time budget for the model;
  - a runner that retries calls and checks before resending;
  - Live Final pre-flight and rehearsal commands.
- **Data hygiene:** repeated claims are dropped sentence by sentence; past order prices are context, not arguments (they "hold, but do not change our calculation" in 41 of 46 replies); our figures go out as an attachment when the supplier asks.

**Changes to earlier requirements:**
- **R5.3:** the deadlock-breaking step is now at least 15% of the gap left, not 0.4% of C.
- **R2.2:** uses the supplier's revealed cost of money once it has priced payment days itself.
- **Acceptance:** targets are now the best recorded run per case, a mean of 70.9.

**Not taken:** `TeamAgent` let the model propose the term sheets and then clamped them back to the plan. In the new agent, code decides every number.

**Unresolved:** the best runs for P02 (0.507) and P11 (0.672) aren't in any agent's log and aren't `TeamAgent`'s. They're probably `BuyerAgent` or `DualAgent` runs with logging off, so I marked those two targets as stretch goals.

### Where the MESO agent was better

From `runs/meso3/` (11 Oct 02:52) and `runs/meso4/` (11 Oct 03:25) on `feature/meso-agent`:

| Case | Type / goal | MESO | Best before | What won it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P11 | quality / quality_first | **0.710** (meso3 and meso4) | 0.672 | Step 1 offered 300 / 800 / 1,500 ppm at equal cost; the supplier took **300 ppm** (the earlier best deal had 1,500 ppm). Step 2 settled the chargeback, then 3 price rounds. Same deal in both runs |
| P18 | raw_material / leverage | **0.453** (meso3) | 0.419 | Step 1: payment 90 / 30 / 45 days at equal cost → 90 locked; step 2: index clause options → locked; then one price round and the final offer at EUR 5.40 |
| P03 | renewal / stabilise | 0.919 (meso3) | 0.919 | Tie with DualAgent's best |

### MESO failures not to repeat

- **P10, 0.0 (meso4):** no coverage move in message 1; the final offer kept 19,890/year for 12
  months, nothing was acceptable, it walked. TeamAgent's 0.671 put the full need for 24 months into
  message 1 (R12.2).
- **P04, 0.056 (meso4):** accepted a 12-month final offer on a 2-year need - the same failure as
  DualAgent's P04 (R11.17, R12.2).
- **P05, 0.0 (meso3):** accepted the best final offer 4.5 minutes after its thread's last move,
  while other threads were still talking; the arena answered `409 Conflict` and the case ended
  without a deal (R13.16).
- **P01, 0.159 (meso4):** every "step" carried a single package (the others fell under the floor),
  so the supplier had no choice to reveal anything; it kept the earliest effective date, a term worth
  EUR 39k, and the deal closed at EUR 137.90 (best runs: 135.20 with the price from April 2027)
  (R13.4).

### DualAgent failures not to repeat

input.new_string:
## 13. From the MESO agent

### 13.1 Settling terms one at a time

- **R13.1 Sequential equal-cost steps for the heavy terms.** After coverage is set (R12.2), rank the
  remaining non-price terms by how many EUR they move C (the playbook's terms first, R13.10), skip any
  under 0.2 % of C, keep at most 3. Each message varies **one** term across up to three packages that
  all cost us the same C; the value the supplier answers with is locked, and the next message varies
  the next term; when every term is locked, only price is left. This is how the R6 sheets are built in
  the first rounds; R6's give / ask / decoy sheets apply in the price rounds and to asked-for terms.
  P11: 300 ppm locked from a 300 / 800 / 1,500 menu → 0.710 twice.
- **R13.2 Option order in a step:** the best option for us first, then the one the supplier asked for
  (if any), its current value, the middle option, the rest - three at most, each a different package.
- **R13.3 Reopen a costly lock.** A term stepped only once whose locked value costs us more than 1 %
  of C against its best option gets one more step (P01: the earliest effective date was worth 3.5 %
  of C).
- **R13.4 A step needs a choice.** A step with fewer than two credible packages (the rest under the
  floor or not cheaper than the supplier's sheet) is not a step: keep the term open, move it to the
  price round with our best value, or skip it - never "lock" a heavy term by sending it alone (P01,
  0.159).
- **R13.5 A term the supplier prices itself is locked without a step** (`revealed`): when its
  e-mail offers two packages that differ in one term only - its sheet and an "Alternatively, with
  30 days: EUR ..." line - lock that term at the value that costs us less at the supplier's own
  prices.
- **R13.6 Read the supplier's prose alternatives** (`prose_alternatives`): "Alternatively, with
  <terms>: EUR <price> per unit" in English and German (Zahlungsziel, Lieferzeit,
  Preisgleitklausel), for payment days, effective date, lead time, volume, contract months, ppm,
  chargeback and Incoterm; a line whose index clause cannot be pinned to an option is skipped. These
  packages feed R12.11 (accept ladder) and R13.5.
- **R13.7 No identical resend.** If the next message would only repeat our last sheets, the thread
  is done (a repeat draws a final offer) - close by R7 or offer back an earlier, cheaper sheet once.

### 13.2 Correct numbers

- **R13.8 Solve the price exactly.** Every package is priced so its C equals the target, not by a
  rule of thumb:
  - without the supplier's margin charge C is linear in the price: `p = (target − C(0)) / (C(1) − C(0))`;
  - with it, C is convex in the price: find the cheapest price by golden-section search between 0.5×
    and 1.5× the supplier's price, and solve for the target by bisection on the side **above** it
    (a price below the cheapest one costs more and leaves the supplier weaker).
  Tests: each sheet of a step has the same C within EUR 1.
- **R13.9 Data arguments computed the way the arena checks them** (`claims.py`): an index change uses
  two months of one series at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data
  (frozen at 2026-09); figures rounded as the sentence states them, next to their IDs. Only arguments
  that argue our side are offered: an index that **rose** confirms the supplier's case and is kept out
  unless it rose less than half the increase asked for (P02, P04). Kinds: index changes, the weighted
  summary of the part's own cost drivers ("explain about +x %, not y %", no ID), a letter giving less
  notice than the contract requires, scorecard quality and delivery, rival quotes and offers,
  should-cost, forecast volume. Each ID once per case; a rival's offer once per supplier.

### 13.3 Playbook per category goal

- **R13.10 One engine, settings per goal** (`PLAYBOOK`):

  | Goal | Anchor (× opening) | Concede | Terms first | Index clause | Margin charge | Walk | Close gap |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | leverage | 0.85 | 0.85 | payment, index | any | no | yes | 0.5 % |
  | routine | 0.90 | 0.80 | contract months, payment | avoid | no | yes | 1.0 % |
  | stabilise | margin-optimal price | 0.80 | volume, contract months, payment | deadband ≥ 3 % | yes | no | 0.5 % |
  | secure_supply | 0.95 | 0.70 | volume, lead time, contract months | avoid | yes | no | 1.5 % |
  | quality_first | 0.92 | 0.80 | ppm, chargeback | avoid | no | yes | 0.5 % |

  The anchors here and in R4.1 must be reconciled into one table before implementation (R4.1's cuts
  come from BuyerAgent and are data-driven; these are MESO's fixed shares). "Walk: no" means:
  stabilise and secure_supply take the best sheet that beats the alternative rather than walk.
- **R13.11 No index clause on a volatile series.** Never offer an index clause on a series that moved
  more than 15 % in its last 12 months - a clause on it is a bet.
- **R13.12 Price-increase anchor:** in a price_increase case the anchor is the current price - no
  increase at all - when it is below the quote.
- **R13.13 Accept on a small gap:** once only price is left, accept when the supplier's C is within
  the playbook's close gap of our target.

### 13.4 The e-mail

- **R13.14 Code writes what must match the sheets** (`writing.py`): the options paragraph is built
  from the term sheets themselves (`describe`: price, payment, effective date, months, volume, lead
  time, index clause with series, share, deadband and base month, ppm, chargeback, Incoterm, tooling),
  so prose and sheets never disagree; code adds its own sentences (a volume commitment, an earlier
  offer taken up) and the signature.
- **R13.15 Lint before sending.** Drop any sentence of the model's that leaks urgency, a deadline, a
  budget, a missing alternative ("no other supplier", "single source", "line stop", "fallback"), our
  limit ("walk-away price", "maximum we", "best we can pay"), "total cost", "category goal" or
  "score"; that carries a data ID; or that states a figure found nowhere in the material. Salutation by
  name only if that name appears in the supplier's e-mails, else "Dear colleagues at <company>". A
  volume question ("which volume can you commit?") is answered by code with the number from our sheet.

### 13.5 Never lose a reply or an accept

- **R13.16 Reply and accept inside 60 s.** A slow POST reads the supplier's reply from the thread
  instead of waiting on the call, so the 60-second rule is not missed (P05 once lost two agreed deals
  to replies held back this way). In an RFQ a final offer that is the best on the table is accepted
  within 60 s of its reply, even while other threads are still talking - waiting for in-flight
  replies (R12.16) never runs past that clock (P05, meso3: accepted after 4.5 minutes → `409`, no deal).
  On a `422` for an accept (the offer moved on) reload the thread and decide again.
- **R13.17 Cached data layer.** Build the master data file once (`arena-build-master-data`) and cache
  each case's negotiation dossier per data revision, so preparation for a case is a cache hit
  (milliseconds) and the Sunday release is picked up automatically.

### Not taken from the MESO agent

- **Locking whatever the supplier picks on a heavy term**, without R13.3/R13.4 (P01, 0.159).
- **The fixed `(1 − concede^k)` curve as the only concession rule** - section 5 (curve, reciprocity,
  deadlock breaker) stays; R13.10's `concede` sets the pace of that curve per goal.

## Acceptance

  under 0.2 % of C, keep at most 3. Each message varies **one** term across up to three packages that
  all cost us the same C; the value the supplier answers with is locked, and the next message varies
  the next term; when every term is locked, only price is left. This is how the R6 sheets are built in
  the first rounds; R6's give / ask / decoy sheets apply in the price rounds and to asked-for terms.
  P11: 300 ppm locked from a 300 / 800 / 1,500 menu → 0.710 twice.
- **R13.2 Option order in a step:** the best option for us first, then the one the supplier asked for
  (if any), its current value, the middle option, the rest - three at most, each a different package.
- **R13.3 Reopen a costly lock.** A term stepped only once whose locked value costs us more than 1 %
  of C against its best option gets one more step (P01: the earliest effective date was worth 3.5 %
  of C).
- **R13.4 A step needs a choice.** A step with fewer than two credible packages (the rest under the
  floor or not cheaper than the supplier's sheet) is not a step: keep the term open, move it to the
  price round with our best value, or skip it - never "lock" a heavy term by sending it alone (P01,
  0.159).
- **R13.5 A term the supplier prices itself is locked without a step** (`revealed`): when its
  e-mail offers two packages that differ in one term only - its sheet and an "Alternatively, with
  30 days: EUR ..." line - lock that term at the value that costs us less at the supplier's own
  prices.
- **R13.6 Read the supplier's prose alternatives** (`prose_alternatives`): "Alternatively, with
  <terms>: EUR <price> per unit" in English and German (Zahlungsziel, Lieferzeit,
  Preisgleitklausel), for payment days, effective date, lead time, volume, contract months, ppm,
  chargeback and Incoterm; a line whose index clause cannot be pinned to an option is skipped. These
  packages feed R12.11 (accept ladder) and R13.5.
- **R13.7 No identical resend.** If the next message would only repeat our last sheets, the thread
  is done (a repeat draws a final offer) - close by R7 or offer back an earlier, cheaper sheet once.

### 13.2 Correct numbers

- **R13.8 Solve the price exactly.** Every package is priced so its C equals the target, not by a
  rule of thumb:
  - without the supplier's margin charge C is linear in the price: `p = (target − C(0)) / (C(1) − C(0))`;
  - with it, C is convex in the price: find the cheapest price by golden-section search between 0.5×
    and 1.5× the supplier's price, and solve for the target by bisection on the side **above** it
    (a price below the cheapest one costs more and leaves the supplier weaker).
  Tests: each sheet of a step has the same C within EUR 1.
- **R13.9 Data arguments computed the way the arena checks them** (`claims.py`): an index change uses
  two months of one series at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data
  (frozen at 2026-09); figures rounded as the sentence states them, next to their IDs. Only arguments
  that argue our side are offered: an index that **rose** confirms the supplier's case and is kept out
  unless it rose less than half the increase asked for (P02, P04). Kinds: index changes, the weighted
  summary of the part's own cost drivers ("explain about +x %, not y %", no ID), a letter giving less
  notice than the contract requires, scorecard quality and delivery, rival quotes and offers,
  should-cost, forecast volume. Each ID once per case; a rival's offer once per supplier.

### 13.3 Playbook per category goal

- **R13.10 One engine, settings per goal** (`PLAYBOOK`):

  | Goal | Anchor (× opening) | Concede | Terms first | Index clause | Margin charge | Walk | Close gap |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | leverage | 0.85 | 0.85 | payment, index | any | no | yes | 0.5 % |
  | routine | 0.90 | 0.80 | contract months, payment | avoid | no | yes | 1.0 % |
  | stabilise | margin-optimal price | 0.80 | volume, contract months, payment | deadband ≥ 3 % | yes | no | 0.5 % |
  | secure_supply | 0.95 | 0.70 | volume, lead time, contract months | avoid | yes | no | 1.5 % |
  | quality_first | 0.92 | 0.80 | ppm, chargeback | avoid | no | yes | 0.5 % |

  The anchors here and in R4.1 must be reconciled into one table before implementation (R4.1's cuts
  come from BuyerAgent and are data-driven; these are MESO's fixed shares). "Walk: no" means:
  stabilise and secure_supply take the best sheet that beats the alternative rather than walk.
- **R13.11 No index clause on a volatile series.** Never offer an index clause on a series that moved
  more than 15 % in its last 12 months - a clause on it is a bet.
- **R13.12 Price-increase anchor:** in a price_increase case the anchor is the current price - no
  increase at all - when it is below the quote.
- **R13.13 Accept on a small gap:** once only price is left, accept when the supplier's C is within
  the playbook's close gap of our target.

### 13.4 The e-mail

- **R13.14 Code writes what must match the sheets** (`writing.py`): the options paragraph is built
  from the term sheets themselves (`describe`: price, payment, effective date, months, volume, lead
  time, index clause with series, share, deadband and base month, ppm, chargeback, Incoterm, tooling),
  so prose and sheets never disagree; code adds its own sentences (a volume commitment, an earlier
  offer taken up) and the signature.
- **R13.15 Lint before sending.** Drop any sentence of the model's that leaks urgency, a deadline, a
  budget, a missing alternative ("no other supplier", "single source", "line stop", "fallback"), our
  limit ("walk-away price", "maximum we", "best we can pay"), "total cost", "category goal" or
  "score"; that carries a data ID; or that states a figure found nowhere in the material. Salutation by
  name only if that name appears in the supplier's e-mails, else "Dear colleagues at <company>". A
  volume question ("which volume can you commit?") is answered by code with the number from our sheet.

### 13.5 Never lose a reply or an accept

- **R13.16 Reply and accept inside 60 s.** A slow POST reads the supplier's reply from the thread
  instead of waiting on the call, so the 60-second rule is not missed (P05 once lost two agreed deals
  to replies held back this way). In an RFQ a final offer that is the best on the table is accepted
  within 60 s of its reply, even while other threads are still talking - waiting for in-flight
  replies (R12.16) never runs past that clock (P05, meso3: accepted after 4.5 minutes → `409`, no deal).
  On a `422` for an accept (the offer moved on) reload the thread and decide again.
- **R13.17 Cached data layer.** Build the master data file once (`arena-build-master-data`) and cache
  each case's negotiation dossier per data revision, so preparation for a case is a cache hit
  (milliseconds) and the Sunday release is picked up automatically.

### Not taken from the MESO agent

- **Locking whatever the supplier picks on a heavy term**, without R13.3/R13.4 (P01, 0.159).
- **The fixed `(1 − concede^k)` curve as the only concession rule** - section 5 (curve, reciprocity,
  deadlock breaker) stays; R13.10's `concede` sets the pace of that curve per goal.

content.text:
I've added the MESO agent to [NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md) as section 13. MESO's own run logs show it set two practice records:

| Case | MESO | Best before | What won it |
|---|---|---|---|
| P11 | **0.710** (in two runs) | 0.672 | It offered 300, 800 or 1,500 ppm at equal cost, and the supplier took 300 ppm. The earlier best deal had 1,500 ppm. |
| P18 | **0.453** | 0.419 | It settled payment first (90 days), then the index clause, then price. |
| P03 | 0.919 | 0.919 | Tie with the best. |

**What section 13 takes, along the lines you guessed (the calculations and the offers):**
- **The offers:**
  - Settle the heavy terms one at a time with up to three equal-cost packages, and lock in the supplier's pick.
  - A locked term that costs us more than 1% of C gets one more step.
  - A term the supplier prices itself in an "Alternatively, with 30 days: €…" line is locked without a step. These lines are read in English and German.
  - Never resend identical sheets.
- **The calculations:**
  - Each package's price is solved exactly so it hits the target cost. All sheets in a step must have the same C within €1.
  - Data arguments are computed the way the arena checks them, and a rising index is kept out because it argues the supplier's case.
- **Per-goal playbook:** the table of anchor, pace, terms first, index stance, margin charge, walk and close gap. Also: no index clause on a series that moved more than 15% in 12 months.
- **The e-mail:** the options paragraph is built from the term sheets, and a lint step removes leaks and invented figures.
- **Never losing a reply or an accept:** if sending is slow, it reads the supplier's reply from the thread instead of waiting, and the master data file is cached.

**MESO's own failures, now listed as rules to avoid:**
- **P10, 0.0:** no full-coverage move in the first message.
- **P04, 0.056:** accepted a 12-month offer on a 2-year need.
